content:
sasha: Ran the smoke runner for redwood-quant-2.1 on staging dashboard; scorecard shows a large negative precision delta for the embeddings cohort — looks wrong, anyone else seeing this?

marta: yep saw it in the morning. sample_count for that cohort is lower than expected and the metric names in the payload look inconsistent.

jay: can you paste the runner command/log that produced it?

sasha: sure -- here's what I ran:
```bash
./eval-runner --mode=smoke --cohort=embeddings --model=redwood-quant-2.1 --seed=42 --exporter=dashboard-json
```

sasha: snippet from the exporter output (trimmed):
```json
{"sample_count": 120, "precision_at_1": 0.63, "precision@5": 0.82, "variant": "q2.1"}
{"sample_count": 0, "p@1": 0.00, "precision@5": 0.79}
```

eval-bot: CI smoke-run finished for 2209876543 — artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/staging/2209876543/smoke.zip :white_check_mark:

eric: hmm looks like a metric-name mismatch. some exporters emit "precision_at_1", others "p@1" or "precision@1". frontend expects canonical keys (p@1) so the diffing logic drops the other field and treats it as missing -> negative delta.

sasha: that's the exact issue. I thought we had normalization in metrics_registry but maybe it regressed after the exporter refactor last week.

marta: short-term we can canonicalize names in the UI layer (map synonyms) and add an alert if sample_count variance > 1%. but long-term fix belongs in runner exporter. @jay can you take a look at the exporter code?

jay: on it. repro'd locally. exporter uses metrics_registry to emit the key from metric.id, but a recent change lets aliases slip through. patching now.

jay: quick diff I'm testing:
```diff
- out[name] = metric.value
+ canonical = metrics_registry.canonical_name(metric.id)
+ out[canonical] = metric.value
```

jay: also noticed drilldown CSV drops "variant" column when sample_count==0, which collapses rows. adding explicit variant col.

sasha: can you also re-run with baseline pinned? I want to confirm the baseline alignment before approving the UI workaround.

eric: +1. Run with --baseline=redwood-2.0-stable and include sample ids. we should capture raw_examples for the failing cohort.

marta: I added a temporary mapping in the scorecard view to surface synonyms and an annotation when sample_count differs by >1%. will push a patch to staging so the dashboard shows both keys until exporter is fixed.

sasha: re-run started by jay. ETA ~ 8 minutes :hourglass: please keep an eye on the sample_count metric.

jay: re-run finished. artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/staging/2209876543/rerun.zip — new export includes canonical keys, variant column, and baseline redwood-2.0-stable.

jay: logs show previous runs had an empty batch collapse that set sample_count to 0 for the alias rows. fixed batching edge-case in exporter.

eric: great. marta — can you remove the temporary UI mapping once we see two clean runs? also add a lightweight test in dashboard_e2e that validates metric key mapping for quantized variants.

marta: will do. added ticket ML-1428 to track removing the mapping and adding the test.

sasha: confirmed numbers look sane now. precision deltas are small and sample counts align. thanks everyone :clap: :rocket: 

eval-bot: smoke re-run succeeded and baseline comparison passed. link: https://console.redwood.ai/evals/2209876543 :eyes:

jay: PR up for exporter fix: https://git.redwood.ai/r/ev/347 — includes canonicalization + variant column + a unit test for empty-batch handling.

marta: planning to roll the UI patch revert after 2 green runs. leaving the alert on for another 24h.

sasha: excellent. closing this thread after rollout. if anyone sees any regression ping me directly.
